newsitem.title: CANADA: Venezuela oil official calls for OPEC reforms.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil official calls for OPEC reforms.

text.p: A top official of Venezuela's state oil company said on Tuesday that OPEC should be reformed to allow members more liberal energy trade in their geographic regions to give them the power to respond to prevailing business conditions.

"It seems that the way business is going on, and the need for energy security in the markets, (there is a) need for a new policy vis-a-vis a new OPEC," Gustavo Inciarte, director of Petroleos de Venzuela SA (PDVSA), told reporters following a speech to an energy conference.
"What we're aiming is to have OPEC re-adapt to the current ways of doing business."

He said further energy integration, such as moves in recent years to align Venezuela's upstream energy industry with downstream markets in the United States and Caribbean countries, would allow the country to become "more self-sufficient on a regional basis".
Inciarte said Venezuela aimed to boost its oil production capacity to 6.1 million barrels per day in 2006 from 3.7 million this year, a 65 percent increase.
However, the surge in production would coincide with an increase in demand and not mean cheating on expected OPEC quotas, he said.
Inciarte echoed statements made by PDVSA President Luis Giusti in Caracas on Tuesday that Venezuela was not producing more oil than its OPEC-mandated quota allowed.
The country has often been cited by traders as flouting its 2.359 million barrel per day OPEC quota.
"We are complying with all the OPEC requirements," Inciarte said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
